originality.rationale: Closest primary material gives pointwise denumerant bounds (Aldrich et al.) or a general polynomial-coefficient algorithm (Baldoni et al.), not the explicit coprimality sign rigidity and inverse-residue sharp density. Direct implication, aliases, algorithms and prior related findings were compared; a general algorithm can indirectly recover the slopes, so hidden or implicit precedence remains a nonzero risk.
residual_risks: The 2013 step-polynomial coefficient algorithms can compute the relevant slopes and might make parts of this formula a derivable corollary; priority of the explicit sign-density classification requires independent review.
Unindexed older papers or broad numerical-semigroup theses could contain an equivalent monotonicity criterion.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the natural structural question whether representation counts increase with every unit step. It gives an if-and-only-if arithmetic boundary for primitive triples, an exact modular-inverse descent frequency for a broad infinite family, positive-density oscillation when multiple pair gcds occur, and the distinct unit-generator boundary. These facts are not consequences of mere quadratic growth and are relevant to restricted partitions and factorization counts.
